newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage bankers say profit margins up in '95.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage bankers say profit margins up in '95.

text.p: The mortgage banking industry's profit margin nearly doubled last year to 8.8 percent for the average firm from 4.6 percent in 1994, the Mortgage Bankers Association of America said Wednesday.
Net operating margin, which is the profit margin before sale of servicing, was 4.5 percent in 1995, up from minus 4.0 percent in 1994, the trade association said.

The study was conducted among 309 mortgage banking companies, which originated nearly 70 percent of all mortgage banking company single-family loan volume. It only measured single-family loan business, MBA said.

"In 1995, mortgage companies were able to register a profit without having to rely so heavily on servicing sales as they did in the more difficult market of 1994," David Lereah, MBA's chief economist, said in a statement.
"The 1995 figure is, nonetheless, a modest profit number historically. While there are signs of progress, profit margins remain relatively narrow," he said.
